result:
The proposed answer of 5 is wrong, and the error is in the enumeration of $P$.

**Where the work goes wrong:** The solution omits the degree 5 of $A_5$. The character degrees of $A_5$ are 1, 3, 3, 4, 5, so the non-linear degrees are 3, 3, 4, 5. Since $\omega(5) = 1$, $A_5$ still satisfies the property, and 5 belongs to $P$. Even using only $A_5$, $P \supseteq \{2, 3, 5\}$, so the sum is at least 10, not 5.

**Further primes:** $PSL(2,8)$ has order 504 and character degrees 1, 7, 7, 7, 7, 8, 9, 9, 9 (sum of squares checks to 504). Every non-linear degree has exactly one prime divisor, so $PSL(2,8) \in \mathcal{G}$ and 7 belongs to $P$. This gives $P \supseteq \{2, 3, 5, 7\}$, with sum at least 17. I did not fully verify the classification of all groups in $\mathcal{G}$, so 17 is a likely value rather than a proven one.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
